capabilities.title: Research a topic across social, community, market, code, paper, news, and web sources within a recent time window
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README overview and skills/last30days/SKILL.md source inventory
capabilities.adaptationNotes: Nexus uses a 30-day query window for fast-moving Feynman research and exposes public news, Hacker News, Polymarket, paper, repository, and web evidence through separate governed lanes. It does not claim the upstream social-account breadth.

capabilities.title: Run source searches in parallel and normalize heterogeneous results into one evidence set
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README positioning and runtime skill workflow

capabilities.title: Rank source material using upvotes, likes, comments, views, market participation, and relevance
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README engagement-scoring description and v3 capability notes
capabilities.reason: Cross-platform engagement units are not comparable evidence quality: a view, vote, comment, star, and market dollar have different denominators and manipulation risks. Nexus keeps engagement as source-local context rather than manufacturing one universal truth score.

capabilities.title: Use an agent judge to synthesize ranked evidence into one grounded, renderer-aware cited brief
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README overview and First-class on OpenAI Codex section
capabilities.adaptationNotes: The Feynman Writer, Verifier, and Reviewer synthesize one bounded cited report while deterministic integrity checks preserve source truth.

capabilities.title: Provide useful keyless coverage for Reddit, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, arXiv, Techmeme, and other supported public sources
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README quickstart and What's new free-source sections
capabilities.adaptationNotes: Nexus provides a narrower reviewed keyless baseline for Hacker News, Polymarket, public papers, public repositories, and web search. Unreviewed scraping and helper-CLI sources are not implied.

capabilities.title: Unlock additional social sources through API keys, account tokens, browser sessions, and optional CLIs
capabilities.sourceEvidence: skills/last30days/SKILL.md environment inventory and README setup notes
capabilities.reason: Nexus will not pool social tokens, account cookies, browser sessions, and third-party CLIs into one research process. Each authenticated source requires its own BYOK, consent, storage, terms, and protected-route review.

capabilities.title: Collect comments, ranked community takes, and video transcripts as first-class research evidence
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README The best comments in every brief section
capabilities.reason: Bulk comment and transcript collection has platform-specific access, copyright, privacy, retention, and quotation rules. Nexus does not scrape or persist that material as a general research source.

capabilities.title: Separate a person's own posts from discussion about them and disambiguate person-focused subqueries
capabilities.reason: Automated cross-platform person profiling can misattribute identities and aggregate sensitive context. RECON remains operator-directed and does not build person dossiers from social discussion.

capabilities.title: Report config sources, planned writes, optional commands, missing keys, expired sessions, and source health before or during research
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README Codex preflight and One doctor command sections
capabilities.reason: Nexus does not install or execute the external Last30Days engine, so its cookies, CLIs, writes, and source adapters have no runtime state to diagnose. Native providers and protected routes retain their own health and status surfaces.

capabilities.title: Install and run through Codex and many Agent Skills hosts with host-specific manifests
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README install and Codex sections plus .codex-plugin metadata
capabilities.reason: Nexus is the host application and does not alter global Codex, Cursor, Claude, or other assistant configuration. Optional external installation remains an operator choice outside the project.

capabilities.title: Package the research engine for MCP and other supported desktop or plugin hosts
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README install variants and mcp directory
capabilities.reason: Nexus already exposes its research tools and protected routes natively. Repackaging a separate Python engine as MCP would duplicate provider, credential, process, and authentication boundaries.

capabilities.title: Allow the external skill to call several model/search providers directly from its own environment
capabilities.reason: Nexus requires every AI call to pass through lib/ai.ts and will not add a duplicate provider-routing authority.

capabilities.title: Reuse browser cookies or account sessions to broaden source access
capabilities.sourceEvidence: README setup and preflight browser-cookie plan plus skill environment inventory
capabilities.reason: The Nexus runtime will not silently extract or reuse browser sessions; any future authenticated source needs explicit, source-specific operator consent and protected storage.
